label: <DEL> step (and late original steps) of short sequences whose early tokens include j/n/0/w
explanation: Sparse unit (~1% of steps). About 65% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (7% of <DEL> steps fire) and 35% on original-phase steps t=3..6, almost always on a first occurrence of the input token; it essentially never fires during the copy phase (except rarely at the first output) or at t<2. Firing depends on sequence content: it is much more likely when the early original tokens include j, n, 0 or w (first_tok=j gives 6.8x lift, n 4.8x, 0 3.6x), and in shorter sequences (L<=6). The strongest examples are short sequences starting with j followed by n/w. No crisp predicate was found: <DEL> alone has precision 0.07 (recall 0.58), and <DEL> & first_tok in {j,n,0,f} reaches only F1 about 0.30 on dev. It looks like a content-dependent accumulator over the first few tokens, not a clean single feature.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: j, 0, f, n; copy phase: n, e, j, 0; input phase: ) and the next token to output (most: n, j, e, 0, z, f; least: v, x, i, 3); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=3, t=5.
